OBSERVATION FIRST: every colorectal fold of mice_impute_lr logged sklearn's `Early stopping criterion not reached` -- 20 of 20 at the time of writing, in results/logs/extra_baselines.log. The reported MICE numbers are therefore a TRUNCATED imputation at sklearn's default max_iter=10, not a converged one. That is the same defect class as the fixed-lambda pFedMe handicap: the comparator loses, and nothing in the record distinguishes losing from not being allowed to finish. A reviewer who knows IterativeImputer will ask, and 'we used the default' is not an answer when the log says the default did not suffice. PREDICTION: max_iter=50 moves colorectal AUPRC by less than 0.002 -- the smallest effect this paper reports anywhere, and the materiality floor already used for the merging results. Reasoning: with 188 columns the chained-equation fit is dominated by the first few sweeps, and the downstream model is logistic regression, which is insensitive to small changes in imputed values for variables it weights weakly. Convergence of the IMPUTER is not the same thing as convergence of the PREDICTION, and it is the prediction that is reported. WITHDRAWAL CONDITION: if the paired difference over the (seed, fold) cells has |median| >= 0.002, or a Wilcoxon signed-rank p < 0.05 with a median favouring max_iter=50, then max_iter=10 is a handicap and EVERY mice_impute_lr number in the paper must be re-run at the converged setting on all four cohorts before any of them is reported. Do not report the truncated numbers with a caveat -- a caveat does not repair a comparison the reader cannot recompute. SCORING: paired WITHIN (seed, fold) cells, never on cohort means; a mean-of-means hid the true sign twice in this project already (Result 108, pFedMe prediction 3). If max_iter=50 ALSO fails to converge, that is informative rather than a failure of this test: it means the stopping criterion is unreachable on this design at any practical budget, and the paper should say so in one sentence instead of implying a converged MICE.
